review_policy: Exercises are AI-generated candidates until a human reviewer sets review.status to 'approved' (use scripts/review_content.py). With BANANA_REQUIRE_REVIEWED_CONTENT=true only approved exercises are served.
difficulty_policy: Relative to the topic: the lowest CEFR level in the topic is easy, the highest is hard (only when the topic spans 3+ levels), everything else medium.

topics.name: Present simple vs present continuous
topics.description: Habits and facts vs actions happening now; stative verbs.

topics.name: Past simple vs present perfect
topics.description: Finished past time vs experience, duration and results connected to now.

topics.name: Prepositions of time and place
topics.description: in / on / at for time and place; verb + preposition patterns.

topics.name: Conditionals
topics.description: Zero, first, second and third conditionals.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Listen! The baby ___ (cry).
exercises.explanation: 'Listen!' shows the action is happening now, so we use the present continuous: is + verb-ing.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: My father ___ (work) in a hospital.
exercises.explanation: A permanent situation uses the present simple. With he/she/it, add -s: works.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Water ___ (boil) at 100 degrees Celsius.
exercises.explanation: Scientific facts use the present simple. Water is singular, so: boils.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: He don't like coffee.
exercises.explanation: With he/she/it, the present simple negative is doesn't (does not) + base verb.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence in the negative form.
exercises.prompt: They play football every Saturday.
accepted_answers: They don't play football every Saturday.
They do not play football every Saturday.
exercises.explanation: Present simple negative with I/you/we/they: don't (do not) + base verb.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Look at those clouds. It ___ (get) dark.
exercises.explanation: A change happening around now uses the present continuous: is getting.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: I am knowing the answer.
exercises.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb (a state, not an action), so it is not normally used in the continuous form.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: We ___ (go) to the cinema last night.
exercises.explanation: 'Last night' is a finished past time, so we use the past simple. Go is irregular: went.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: When I was a child, I ___ (not / like) vegetables.
exercises.explanation: A finished past period ('when I was a child') uses the past simple. Negative: didn't + base verb.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: I ___ (visit) Paris three times, and I want to go again.
exercises.explanation: Life experience with no finished time mentioned uses the present perfect: have + past participle.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: I have seen that film yesterday.
exercises.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time. The present perfect cannot be used with it; use the past simple.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: She ___ (live) here since 2015.
exercises.explanation: 'Since' + a starting point describes a situation that began in the past and continues now: present perfect (simple or continuous).

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: He has finished his homework two hours ago.
accepted_answers: He finished his homework two hours ago.
exercises.explanation: 'Two hours ago' refers to a finished past time, so we use the past simple, not the present perfect.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence so it means the same. Use 'for'.
exercises.prompt: I started learning English five years ago, and I am still learning it.
accepted_answers: I have been learning English for five years.
I've been learning English for five years.
I have learned English for five years.
I've learned English for five years.
I have learnt English for five years.
I've learnt English for five years.
exercises.explanation: An action that started in the past and continues now uses the present perfect (continuous) + for + a period of time.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with a, an, the, or - (no article).
exercises.prompt: I saw ___ elephant at the zoo.
exercises.explanation: Use 'an' before a vowel sound. 'Elephant' starts with a vowel sound and is mentioned for the first time.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with a, an, the, or - (no article).
exercises.prompt: Could you close ___ door, please?
exercises.explanation: Both speakers know which door is meant, so we use 'the'.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: My sister is a engineer.
exercises.explanation: 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so the article is 'an'.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with a, an, the, or - (no article).
exercises.prompt: She is ___ university student.
exercises.explanation: The choice depends on sound, not spelling. 'University' starts with a /j/ (you) sound, so we use 'a'.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with a, an, the, or - (no article).
exercises.prompt: He plays ___ guitar in a band.
exercises.explanation: We usually use 'the' with musical instruments after 'play'.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with a, an, the, or - (no article).
exercises.prompt: ___ honesty is important in a friendship.
exercises.explanation: Abstract uncountable nouns used in a general sense take no article.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: The Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
accepted_answers: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
exercises.explanation: Names of single mountains take no article (but mountain ranges do: the Himalayas).

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition.
exercises.prompt: My birthday is ___ May.
exercises.explanation: Use 'in' with months, years and seasons.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition.
exercises.prompt: The meeting starts ___ 9 o'clock.
exercises.explanation: Use 'at' with clock times.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition.
exercises.prompt: He was born ___ 1998.
exercises.explanation: Use 'in' with years.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition.
exercises.prompt: We are having a party ___ Saturday evening.
exercises.explanation: Use 'on' with days, including a day + part of the day (on Saturday evening).

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition.
exercises.prompt: She lives ___ the third floor.
exercises.explanation: Use 'on' with floors of a building.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: I will meet you in the bus stop.
accepted_answers: I will meet you at the bus stop.
I'll meet you at the bus stop.
exercises.explanation: Use 'at' for a point or place where something happens, such as a bus stop.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: We arrived to London late at night.
accepted_answers: We arrived in London late at night.
exercises.explanation: We say 'arrive in' a city or country and 'arrive at' a building or point, never 'arrive to'.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the adjective in brackets.
exercises.prompt: An elephant is ___ (big) than a horse.
exercises.explanation: Short adjectives take -er. With consonant-vowel-consonant endings, double the last consonant: big -> bigger.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: My brother is more tall than me.
accepted_answers: My brother is taller than me.
My brother is taller than I am.
My brother is taller than I.
exercises.explanation: One-syllable adjectives take -er, not 'more': tall -> taller.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the adjective in brackets.
exercises.prompt: This is the ___ (good) pizza I have ever eaten.
exercises.explanation: 'Good' is irregular: good -> better -> best. 'The ... I have ever' needs the superlative.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the adjective in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Today is ___ (hot) day of the year.
exercises.explanation: Comparing one day with all the others needs the superlative with 'the': the hottest (double the t).

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the adjective in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Travelling by train is ___ (comfortable) than travelling by bus.
exercises.explanation: Long adjectives (three or more syllables) use 'more' + adjective.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: This book is more interesting that the film.
accepted_answers: This book is more interesting than the film.
exercises.explanation: Comparatives are followed by 'than', not 'that'.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence so it means the same. Use 'faster'.
exercises.prompt: My car is not as fast as your car.
accepted_answers: Your car is faster than my car.
Your car is faster than mine.
exercises.explanation: 'Not as ... as' can be rephrased with a comparative from the other side: Your car is faster than mine.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: If you heat ice, it ___ (melt).
exercises.explanation: Zero conditional for general truths: if + present simple, present simple.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ (stay) at home.
exercises.explanation: First conditional for a real future possibility: if + present simple, will + base verb.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: If I ___ (have) more money, I would buy a new laptop.
exercises.explanation: Second conditional for an unreal present situation: if + past simple, would + base verb.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: If I will see him, I will tell him.
accepted_answers: If I see him, I will tell him.
If I see him, I'll tell him.
exercises.explanation: In the first conditional, the if-clause uses the present simple, not 'will'.

exercises.instruction: The sentence has one grammar mistake. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.prompt: If she would study harder, she would pass the exam.
accepted_answers: If she studied harder, she would pass the exam.
If she studied harder, she'd pass the exam.
exercises.explanation: In the second conditional, the if-clause uses the past simple, not 'would'.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: If we had left earlier, we ___ (not / miss) the train.
exercises.explanation: Third conditional for an unreal past: if + past perfect, would (not) have + past participle.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence so it means the same. Start with 'If I knew'.
exercises.prompt: I don't know her number, so I can't call her.
accepted_answers: If I knew her number, I could call her.
If I knew her number, I would call her.
If I knew her number, I'd call her.
If I knew her number, I would be able to call her.
If I knew her number, I'd be able to call her.
exercises.explanation: An unreal present situation uses the second conditional: if + past simple, could/would + base verb.
